newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson sale hinges on commission ruling - minister.
newsitem.headline: Thomson sale hinges on commission ruling - minister.

text.p: The government's plan for the privatisation of electronics group Thomson SA hinges on the approval of the French privatisation commission, Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure said on Wednesday.

Lamassoure, who is also government spokesman, told France Inter radio that the government did not expect to review its decision "unless the privatisation commission's conclusion doesn't conform, and then we would have to start again from scratch".
The government said on October 16 that it favoured a takeover proposal from Lagardere for Thomson.

It plans to recapitalise Thomson with 11 billion francs ($2.2 billion) before selling it to Lagardere for one franc. Lagardere in turn plans to sell Thomson's consumer electronics business Thomson Multimedia (TMM) to Daewoo Electronics for one franc.
The terms of the privatisation have triggered an outcry from opposition politicians, union leaders and Thomson workers.

Alcatel Alsthom, which had put in a rival bid for Thomson, has added to the controversy by stressing that its proposal was not identical to Lagardere's and that it would not have sold control of TMM to a foreign group but would have created a 50-50 venture.
Lamassoure said both Alcatel and Lagardere demanded an 11 billion franc recapitalisation in their proposals, and he reiterated that Thomson had run up 28 billion francs of debt.

He said Prime Minister Alain Juppe's decision, announced on Tuesday, to hold a public debate in parliament after the privatisation commission's ruling should clarify the privatisation plan and its industrial implications.
The commission's decision is expected in December.
Asked whether a parliamentary vote would be held after the debate, Lamassoure replied: "Debates are not normally followed by a vote; only draft bills are (followed by a vote)."

Lamassoure said the Thomson deal would be examined not only by the privatisation commission, whose brief is to ensure that the government's financial interest is respected in any privatisation, but also the European Commission.
It must ensure that the French government's recapitalisation does not render Thomson "abnormally competitive" relative to its European and U.S. competitors, Lamassoure said.
